Review of 1.24.35's float switches (wip commit 9820186 against 1.24.34 as released, 1e318a5), 2026-11-23.
A reviewer who wrote none of the change. Inputs and verdicts were written from what each part or circuit IS, before
Lantern was run on them; nothing under src/ or the existing tests was touched.

How to replay
  node tests/fixtures/float_review_1235/replay.js [path/to/lantern.inner.html] [--only <id regex>]
     192 cases (cases_a.js .. cases_e.js), the draft and 1.24.34 loaded side by side in jsdom (lib.js, load.js).
     On the draft:            138 AGREE, 54 DISAGREE (high 21, medium 23, low 10)  -- run_9820186.txt
     The same cases, 1.24.34: 151 AGREE, 41 DISAGREE (high 18, medium 19, low 4)
     Of those, 36 cases went DISAGREE -> AGREE (the drawings, LS with no name, "Lead Pump On"), and 49 went AGREE ->
     DISAGREE (all in the part reader, AI_STATION's FTAG/FJOB2).
  python3 tests/fixtures/float_review_1235/replay_browser.py <out dir>
     draws render_inputs.js's 12 ladders in Chromium with the built page (site/index.html) and with 1.24.34's
     (git show 1e318a5:site/), each process switch at 3x with DRAW's own render (the one Save PNG uses), and contact
     sheets, draft left, 1.24.34 right. The sheets made are in png/ (sheet_00..05.png; preview_size_draft_then_1.24.34.png
     is the Chat preview's own pixels at 3x: rows 1 and 3 the draft, 2 and 4 1.24.34; station-typical-draft.png the
     station's whole ladder as Chat shows it).

==== HIGH ===========================================================================================================

H1. FJOB2 makes switches that are not floats into floats -- on/off switches, selectors (even ones typed "selector
    switch"), push buttons (PB tag, "pushbutton switch" type), e-stops written "Emergency-Stop" / "Emergency Off" /
    "Emergency", lead/lag selectors, two-speed selectors -- and where the station has no float for that job, DRAWS one
    of them as the float.
    Cases: C-onoff, C-pump1-onoff, C-on-dash-off, C-off-on, C-alarm-onoff, C-ss-off, C-selector-type-off,
    C-selector-type-off-s, C-ss-leadlag, C-selector-leadlag, C-ss-pump1-lead, C-ss-pump2-lead, C-ss-lead-pump-1-2,
    C-pb-pump1-off, C-pb-off, C-pb-lead-start, C-pb-lag-start, C-pushbutton-switch-off, C-estop-hyphen, C-estop-off,
    C-estop-emergency, C-highlow-speed, C-hi-lo, C-pump1-off-s, E-lead-and-lag, E-pump-hash-off, E-sensor-pump1-off;
    what is drawn: C-set-onoff-is-not-the-off-float, C-set-estop-is-not-the-off-float,
    C-set-leadlag-selector-is-not-the-lag, C-set-no-floats-onoff-estop.
    Seen (draft; every one of these was "not carried" on 1.24.34):
      - part ES1 switch "Emergency-Stop" beside LS2 lead, LS3 lag, LS4 alarm: the station's off float is ES1, and Lantern
        tells the person: "As the water rises to LS2 (Lead On), the lead pump starts; it pumps the well down to ES1
        (Emergency-Stop) and stops." The ladder draws ES1 as a normally open float in both call relays' rungs.
      - part S1 switch "On/Off" the same: "it pumps the well down to S1 (On/Off) and stops".
      - part SS1 selector switch "Lead/Lag" beside off, lead and alarm floats: drawn as the lag float SS1 (1.24.34 drew
        three floats and said there is no lag float).
      - part SW2 switch "Alarm On/Off" and part ES1 switch "Emergency": drawn as a second high level alarm float.
      - pumps with part S1 switch "On/Off" and part S2 switch "Emergency Stop", no floats: 1.24.34 drew the schematic;
        now it is read as a station whose off float is S1, with a lead float Lantern made.
      - beside a station that already has the job, the summary says e.g. "not drawn: S1 “On/Off” (the station has one
        off float: both pumps stop on it)" -- telling the reader the on/off switch is a float.
    Traced to (src/lantern.inner.html, AI_STATION partRole):
      (a) FJOB2's word set holds on, off, stop, pump(s), digits, "/" and "&", so "On/Off", "Pump 1 On/Off", "Off",
          "High/Low", "Hi-Lo", "Lead/Lag", "Lead & Lag", "Pump 1 Lead" all pass, and each has off/lead/lag/high/low in it;
      (b) the exclusion /\b(?:hand|auto|...|selector|...|push|e-?stop)\b|\bemergency\s+stop\b/ is tested on the name
          (lb) only -- a part typed "selector switch" or "pushbutton switch" with the name "Off" passes;
      (c) "\bemergency\s+stop\b" misses "Emergency-Stop"; "Emergency Off" and "Emergency" are not excluded (floatJob
          reads "emergency" as the high level alarm, "emergency ... off" as the off float);
      (d) the tag is never asked: PB (push button), SS (selector), ES (e-stop), SW, HS are not a float's, by the same
          JIC/NFPA reading that made LS a limit switch.
    Expected: each of these is not a float ("not carried", as on 1.24.34); a station missing a float gets the usual
    one, said, as Lantern already does when no float is written.

H2. LS-tagged floats named with start, stop or on are no longer floats, and the station drawn runs differently from
    the one the model wrote -- among them Adam's own probes written as switches.
    Cases: C-ls-stop, C-ls-start, C-ls-on, C-ls-pump-on, C-ls-pump1-on, C-ls-pump2-on, C-ls-both-on, C-ls-all-on,
    C-ls-1st-on, C-ls-second-start, C-ls-pump1-start; what is drawn: C-set-adam-probes-as-switches, C-set-pump-on,
    C-set-on-both, C-set-start-stop, C-set-pump-off-on.
    Seen (draft; 1.24.34 read every set as written):
      - LS1 "Stop", LS2 "Start", LS3 "High": drawn FS1 off (Lantern's), LS3 "High" as the LEAD float, LS1 and LS2 "not
        carried ... (switch)"; "no lag float: one pump runs at a time". Adam (2026-11-23): High should start the second
        pump while the first runs. As probes (E1-E3) or as FS switches the same three read off, lead, lag (E-probes-*,
        E-fs-*: right); only the LS form changed.
      - LS1 "Pumps Off", LS2 "Pump 1 On", LS3 "Pump 2 On", LS4 "High Water Alarm": the lag float is lost (LS1 off,
        FS1 lead made by Lantern, LS4 alarm); the second pump never runs on high water.
      - LS1 "Pump Off", LS2 "Pump On", LS3 "Both Pumps On", LS4 "High Level": LS4 "High Level" becomes the lead start.
      - nothing goes back to the model: the floats it wrote are listed under "not carried".
    Traced to: FTAG no longer takes LS, and FJOB2 requires lead|lag|off|alarm|high|low|hi|lo|emergency in the name, so
    a name of start/stop/on words alone ("Stop", "Pump 2 On", "Both Pumps On") is neither.
    Expected: Adam's rule holds where the part is a limit switch's -- LS with no name, or named hatch, valve, door,
    open, closed (C-ls-noname, C-ls-hatch-*, C-ls-valve-open, C-ls-open/closed, C-set-ls-noname: all AGREE now) -- but
    an LS on a lift station's schematic whose whole name is a float's job, start/stop/on included, is a float (no limit
    switch on a station is called "Pump 2 On" or "Both Pumps On"). For a plain S tag, start and stop stay buttons
    (C-start, C-stop, C-pump1-start, C-pump1-stop AGREE): the tag is what tells them apart.

==== MEDIUM ==========================================================================================================

M1. B-cutout-written-without-nc (medium) and B-thermostat-heater-written-without-nc (low): not this change's doing,
    but this change makes it show. A model that writes `pressure PS1 M1 "high pressure cutout"` (no nc; the prompt
    says "write nc for a normally closed one") gets a compressor that never starts (runs 0: 4: 6:M1). On 1.24.34 the
    picture (blade up, diaphragm pushing it further open) looked like a cutout while the circuit treated it as
    normally open; now picture and circuit agree, so the drawing shows a switch that closes on rising pressure under
    the word "cutout". A "cutout"/"cut-out" pressure or temperature switch (or a heater's thermostat) written without
    nc is a case for rule 3: back once with `pressure PS1 M1 nc "high pressure cutout"`.

==== LOW =============================================================================================================

L1. B-control-two-alarms-one-horn: in a branch row (e.under) the tag is drawn 30 under the switch and crosses the
    float (the float's ring reaches y+25, "FS5" at 12 px starts at about y+24.6; sheet: duplex-two-alarms-horn-FS5).
    1.24.34 the same; the change moved the row's label clear of the float (y+34) but not the branch row's tag.
L2. E-isa-lshl, E-isa-lsa: FTAG also dropped LSHL (ISA level switch high-low), LSA and LSW, which 1.24.34 took as
    floats (and asked their jobs); the change's comment names only LS. Now "not carried" without a word.
L3. A-palette-has-float: Draw's Electrical palette has Limit switch NO/NC but no float, pressure or temperature
    switch, so a person drawing a lift station's ladder by hand cannot place the symbol AI_CONTROL draws. A gap, not a
    regression.
L4. E-station-floats-low-shorthand: "floats low off lead lag alarm" in MAKE STATION drops "low" without a word (the
    long form, float FS0 "low level alarm", is drawn, normally closed: E-station-low-alarm-nc AGREE). Not this change.
L5. For Adam's eye (no case fails): the normally closed blade rises 4 px over 26; in Chat's preview (scale 0.76 to 0.80 for these
    ladders) that is about 3 px, and at that size it reads as a T resting on the terminal (png/preview_size_*.png). Distinct
    from normally open (blade down), but the lean is slight.

==== WHAT THE CHANGE GOT RIGHT (AGREE) ===============================================================================

- The symbols (A, 32 cases): float, pressure and temperature, normally open: the blade under the line, clear of the
  right terminal, the float/diaphragm/bulb under it on a stem that meets the blade; normally closed: the blade resting
  on the right terminal's top, its end beyond it. Ports unchanged; contact, button, toggle, limit, overload, coil, lamp,
  solenoid, horn, fuse drawn exactly as on 1.24.34; the limit switch keeps the selector's blade.
- Every circuit (B, 21 cases), simulated through the process's rise and fall with "normally open = closes as the
  process rises" (the usual meaning of normal for a process switch: least stimulus -- an empty well, no pressure,
  cold): the station (4 floats; 24 V DC with a horn; no lag), MAKE CONTROL's duplex example, two alarm lights, two
  alarm floats on one horn, the low level alarm (the one normally closed float a station draws, its light lit only
  below it), a simplex sump, the prompt's sump example, a fill (nc), a booster's low level cutoff, a compressor's high
  pressure cutout (nc) with and without buttons, a low suction pressure cutout, a heater's thermostat and high limit
  (nc), a fan's thermostat (no), a motor overtemperature switch, four process switches on one rung. Each runs as it
  should, each contact is drawn the way the circuit uses it, its tag and label clear of other strokes -- and the
  circuits are 1.24.34's exactly. On 1.24.34 every one of these was drawn the wrong way up (normally open: blade up,
  a rising float pushing it further open; normally closed: blade under the terminal with the stem through it), and the
  labels under floats touched the float.
- The part reader: LS with no name or a limit's name is not a float (Adam); "Lead Pump On" on an S tag now is; ISA
  LSL/LSH/LSHH/LSLL, FS, float/level types and names, the 35B's sensors, Adam's probes Stop/Start/High (High the lag)
  as before; start/stop buttons, HOA, hand/auto, alarm silence/reset/test, speed, oil, temperature, lights, relays,
  horns, breakers and lead/lag "select"/"selector" names are not floats.

==== THE GUARD (D, 6 cases, all AGREE) ===============================================================================

- Every bench question of both sets (150 + 150) is offered the tools 1.24.34 offered it.
- 1,221 saved replies (944 rows of tests/fixtures/bench_run_*.json, first and last) build as on 1.24.34: ok, kind,
  readAs, problems, summary, and the ladder's rungs and contacts.
- 944 rows solved the bench's way and graded: each passes or fails as on 1.24.34. 66 ideals: the same, and
  make-liftstation(-b) and make-control(-b) pass.
- 6 saved replies draw a ladder; 3 are drawn differently, and only in process switches' lines and circles and the
  label under one.
- Not a case here, but run: the three reviews of 1.24.34 (liftstation_review1/2/3_1234, 752 cases) give the same
  verdict, line for line, on the draft as on 1.24.34.
- No difference was found in any bench question or saved reply: the 49 regressions above are all inputs of this
  review's own (no saved reply has a part-and-wire schematic with these names).

==== THE PROJECT'S OWN TESTS ON THE DRAFT ============================================================================

- npm test was started and stopped by this reviewer's 20-minute limit after 54 suites, all PASS, none failed; the rest
  of it was not run as a whole. Run on their own, all PASS: tests/control.js, liftstation.js, station.js,
  liftstation_1234.js, float_switch_1235.js, and the nine replayed reviews of 1.24.30, 1.24.31 and 1.24.34
  (review*_liftstation_1230.py, review*_station_1231.py, review*_liftstation_1234.py).

==== NOT RUN ===========================================================================================================

- No model was run: no bench on the 35B or the small models; every reply here is scripted.
- The Draw page itself was not clicked (Open in Draw, Save PNG); the pictures were made with DRAW's render(), which
  Save PNG uses, and AI_DRAW's preview.
- The JIC/NEMA chart itself (the blade's exact angle) was not opened; the meaning of "normal" (least stimulus) was
  checked against Kuphaldt, Lessons In Industrial Instrumentation, "Process switches"
  (https://ibiblio.org/kuphaldt/socratic/sinst/output/process_switches.pdf). How the symbols look to a tradesman is
  Adam's to judge (png/).
